messages:
alex.k: Heads-up — seeing a flood of inference-queue-latency pages since ~03:00 UTC, ~60 pagers so far. Seems like short spikes rather than sustained degradation. Anyone else?

maya: Yeah I saw them too. Dashboard here: https://redwood.app/dashboards/infra/queue-latency — spikes line up with a few small batch jobs.

jordan: I think the alert is too sensitive (1m avg + median). Proposal: switch to p95 over 10m and increase the `for` window to reduce flapping. Also consider demoting to warning unless >5% of hosts affected.

alex.k: Current alert rule in alerts repo looks like this:
```
ALERT InferenceQueueLatencyHigh
  IF histogram_quantile(0.5, sum(rate(inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket[1m])) by (le, job)) > 0.2
  FOR 5m
  LABELS { severity="page" }
```

maya: Suggest new rule snippet:
```
ALERT InferenceQueueLatencyElevated
  IF histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket[10m])) by (le, job)) > 0.5
  FOR 10m
  LABELS { severity="warning" }
```
Also add runbook label: runbook_url=https://redwood.app/runbooks/queue-latency

jordan: To avoid pages for single-host blips we can gate paging on affected hosts fraction. Example idea (needs validation):
```
affected_hosts = count_values("host", increase(inference_request_errors_total[10m]))
if (affected_hosts / count(instances) > 0.05) -> page else -> warn
```
Not exact PromQL, but we can compute host-counts and add as an additional condition in the PR.

alex.k: Can someone open an alerts PR with the p95+10m change and add the runbook link? Also request a 1h silence while we finalize so on-call isn't flooded. I'm going to be offline at 11:30 UTC.

sre-oncall: I can create a temporary silence. @alerts-bot can you schedule a 60m mute for the rule `InferenceQueueLatencyHigh` in prod?

alerts-bot: Silence created: https://redwood.app/silences/si-12345 — expires in 60 minutes. Notifying on-call. :white_check_mark:

maya: Thanks. I'll open the PR with the exact PromQL and move severity to warning; include a note about host-fraction gating and link to the dashboard/runbook.

jordan: I'll pair-review the PR and help test on staging. After merge we should watch the dashboard for 2 hours, then decide if further threshold tuning is needed.

alex.k: Perfect — appreciate it. If it still flaps after the PR we can add grouping by region/instance and tighten host-fraction logic.
